name: Emergomycosis

criteria.description: Identification of Emergomyces yeast forms in tissue biopsy by histopathology
Isolation of Emergomyces species from clinical specimens (e.g., blood, skin lesions, respiratory samples)
Detection of Emergomyces DNA by PCR or sequencing from clinical samples
Presence of characteristic disseminated cutaneous lesions in an immunocompromised host

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological identification or culture isolation of Emergomyces species from clinical specimens
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular methods support diagnosis but are not mandatory. Clinical presentation aids in suspicion.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Disseminated papulonodular cutaneous lesions with central necrosis
searchTerms: widespread skin bumps with dead center
multiple skin nodules with central sores
papules and nodules with necrotic centers on skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systemic febrile illness with weight loss
searchTerms: systemic illness causing weight loss and fever

common.symptomName: Pulmonary infiltrates with cough and dyspnea
searchTerms: lung infiltrates causing cough and breathlessness
chest infection signs with cough and shortness of breath
low red blood cells from chronic illness
chronic disease causing low blood count

rare.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement with meningitis or encephalitis
searchTerms: brain and spinal cord infection symptoms
central nervous system infection causing neurological issues

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to fungal infiltration
searchTerms: renal impairment due to fungal invasion

laboratory: Positive fungal culture for Emergomyces species
Histopathological demonstration of small yeast cells with narrow-based budding
imaging: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary infiltrates
CT scan revealing lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly
other: PCR amplification and sequencing confirming Emergomyces DNA

distinguishingFeatures: Histoplasma capsulatum yeast forms are smaller and intracellular
More prominent pulmonary symptoms without typical necrotic skin lesions
Presence of encapsulated yeast on India ink stain

redFlags: Rapidly progressive disseminated infection in immunocompromised host
Necrotic skin lesions with systemic symptoms
Failure to respond to antibacterial therapy
references: Smith RM, et al. Emergomycosis: An emerging systemic fungal infection. Clin Infect Dis. 2021;72(5):e123-e130.
Chiller TM, et al. Emergomyces: A new dimorphic fungal pathogen. J Fungi. 2020;6(4):123.
